article_title: Fostering Early Numerical Skills at School Start in Children at Risk for Mathematical Achievement Problems: A Small Sample Size Training Study
citation: Marcus Hasselhorn & Kathrin Linke-Hasselhorn. (2013). Fostering Early Numerical Skills at School Start in Children at Risk for Mathematical Achievement Problems: A Small Sample Size Training Study. International Education Studies, 6(3). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/ies.v6n3p213
title: MZZ training program "Mengen, zählen, Zahlen" (Krajewski, Nieding, & Schneider, 2007)
description: MZZ is a German training program promoting early awareness of quantities, numbers and relations between numbers. The article describes it as one that "systematically builds up conceptual knowledge from practising basic skills to instruction in numerical structures" and "offers a clear structure of the numerical space, allowing for effective problem solving strategies". Children use graspable materials that represent the structure of numbers, so the abstract structure is rendered "tangible" and "visible". The program comprises three focal areas corresponding to competence levels I through III, delivered playfully in small groups; the manual specifies 24 sessions of 30 minutes.
requirements: The MZZ authors recommend application in small groups of up to six children to support particularly weak children at kindergarten
constraints: The article notes the program's evaluation suggests training should best be conducted shortly before school start to increase the probability of transfer to school achievement
target_learners: pre-school class children deferred from school entry with weak number competencies
examples: In this study the program was run in a separate room three times per week during regular lessons, in 24 sessions of 30 minutes with a playful atmosphere
key_sources: Marcus Hasselhorn & Kathrin Linke-Hasselhorn. (2013). Fostering Early Numerical Skills at School Start in Children at Risk for Mathematical Achievement Problems: A Small Sample Size Training Study. International Education Studies, 6(3). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/ies.v6n3p213

article_title: Investigating transfer of learning in advanced quantum mechanics
citation: Maries, A., Sayer, R., and Singh, C. (2015). Investigating transfer of learning in advanced quantum mechanics. https://scholar.google.com
title: Research-based MZI tutorial with thought experiments and an interactive simulation
description: The research-based Mach-Zehnder Interferometer tutorial is the instructional element preceding the transfer questions. The article states that it "uses thought experiments and an interactive simulation" and helps students learn wave-particle duality of single photons, interference of a single photon with itself, the probabilistic nature of quantum measurements, and collapse of a quantum state upon measurement. Students manipulate the MZI setup in the interactive simulation to predict and observe detector outcomes for various polarizer configurations, learning how polarizer orientations affect interference via WPI considerations.
requirements: Students work through the tutorial before answering the analogous DSE transfer questions, and complete the accompanying MZI pre-/post-test with polarizers of various orientations in one or both paths.
target_learning_goals: interference of a single photon with itself
collapse of a quantum state upon measurement
key_sources: Maries, A., Sayer, R., and Singh, C. (2015). Investigating transfer of learning in advanced quantum mechanics. https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.07570

article_title: Developing an Interactive Tutorial on a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer with Single Photons
citation: Chandralekha Singh and Emily Marshman. (2014). Developing an Interactive Tutorial on a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer with Single Photons. 2014 PERC Proceedings. https://doi.org/10.1119/perc.2014.pr.056
title: Quantum Interactive Learning Tutorial (QuILT) on a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer with single photons
description: The QuILT is an interactive tutorial exposing "upper-level students in quantum mechanics courses to contemporary applications" via "gedanken (thought) experiments and simulations involving a MZI with single photons." It covers wave-particle duality of a single photon, single-photon interference, probabilistic quantum measurement, and state collapse, and how detectors and beam-splitters affect outcomes. It "makes use of a computer simulation in which students can manipulate the MZI setup to predict and observe what happens at the detectors for different setups."
requirements: Uses a guided approach to learning
A warmup with background information about the MZI setup with a beam of light and pre-/posttests given before and after the QuILT
constraints: Simplifying assumptions: all optical elements are ideal, beam-splitters infinitesimally thin, photons travel the same distance in vacuum in both paths, and the initial setup gives constructive interference at D1 and destructive interference at D2
target_learning_goals: wave-particle duality of a single photon
interference of a single photon with itself
collapse of a quantum state upon measurement
examples: Different versions were iterated with three physics faculty members and administered to graduate and upper-level undergraduate students to check clarity before in-class evaluation
key_sources: Chandralekha Singh and Emily Marshman. (2014). Developing an Interactive Tutorial on a Mach-Zehnder Interferometer with Single Photons. 2014 PERC Proceedings. https://doi.org/10.1119/perc.2014.pr.056
